findings.reason: §3 is the design's statement of the contract, and as written it teaches a tag the writer deletes and omits ones the schema requires, so it must cite the schema owner or be corrected against it.
findings.text: §3's head-scalar table forks the meta contract owned by `reckon/_schema.py:1175` and `docs/_shared/plan.schema.json`, and the fork has already drifted on three points, so an author following §3 writes tags the code does not accept: (a) line 93 lists `plan-tier` as author-owned, but `reckon/_plan_html.py:1783` strips it on every write whenever `tier` is absent from state; (b) line 91 gives `plan-effort` with value `M`, while the owner emits `plan-effort-hours` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:1754`) and `_schema.py:1175` carries `effort_hours`; (c) it omits `plan-tags` (used by the `reckon-create` fast path and present in `plan.schema.json`) and the `plan-capability-*` metas.

findings.reason: the contract is meant to be exhaustive ("every tag, and WHY"), and a set that silently drops one of six owned sections misdirects the author it exists for.
findings.text: §3's body-section list restates the six `data-reckon` section spellings but names only five, omitting `gates`; the owner `reckon/_plan_html.py:548` (`SECTION_IDS`) and `reckon/_plan_html.py:1640` (`_SECTION_RECOGNISED_SPELLING`, `'gates': '<div class="r-gate" data-id="...">'`) both carry it, so a section the parser recognises and the write-guard names is absent from the design's contract.

findings.reason: the plan's own §9 argues for one exemplar over many restatements, so §4 either defers to `docs/_exemplar-plan.html` or is the drift the plan is trying to prevent.
findings.text: §4 re-derives copyable markup for a decision (`div.r-dec`, line 139) and a followup (`article.r-fu`, line 150) that `docs/_exemplar-plan.html` already owns as the canonical annotated source, and that `skills/reckon-create/SKILL.md:32-35` and `skills/reckon-edit/SKILL.md:26-31` point authors at for exactly this purpose; three owners of one spelling means the §5 rule "reuse the exact class/attr names from §4" can silently disagree with the others.

findings.reason: a recommendation that re-proposes landed machinery reads as open work and invites a duplicate re-implementation, so each §9 bullet should cite the owner that already provides it or state what remains.
findings.text: §9 recommends shipping "a single canonical authoring prompt" (line 243) and "one self-describing exemplar in-repo `docs/_exemplar-plan.html`" (line 247) as new work, but both already exist and are wired into the skills: `docs/_exemplar-plan.html` is present, and `skills/reckon-create/SKILL.md:32-35` and `skills/reckon-edit/SKILL.md:26-31` already declare it "the canonical annotated exemplar … copy the matching specimen"; the CI round-trip parity test §9 recommends (line 252) already exists as `tests/test_schema.py::test_state_round_trip`.

findings.reason: the reframe (MCP optional, not mandatory) is a decision already locked at line 275 and does not turn on the exact tool count, so naming the file would sharpen the prose without changing the design.
findings.text: §1/§8 describe the "~19 MCP tools" surface and its costs from memory, and §8 reframes them, but neither section opens `reckon/mcp.py` to name which tools actually exist or which the plan would retire, so the "optional version-safe writer" recommendation has no census of the surface it is judging.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §9 concentrates the whole tag/template contract behind one prompt plus one exemplar ("prompt-first, tool-second"), a small interface over a large body of contract, rather than a spread of per-field wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 re-states the machine-readable contract owned by `reckon/_schema.py` plus `docs/_shared/plan.schema.json`, and §4 re-derives markup owned by `docs/_exemplar-plan.html` and the section spellings owned by `reckon/_plan_html.py:1640`; the fork has already drifted.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families: 23; no section adds to any of the four families, and the one interface-shaped proposal (§10 milestone tooling) resolved to `edit_plan(create=True, doc_type="milestone")`, an extension of the existing typed-resource path that retires no CLI option or MCP view.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan re-proposes the canonical authoring prompt and the in-repo exemplar as its own recommendations (§9, lines 243-247) without citing `skills/reckon-create/SKILL.md:32-35`, `skills/reckon-edit/SKILL.md:26-31` or `docs/_exemplar-plan.html`, which already carry them.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the design removes a mandatory layer (the MCP as the only door) and adds no new wrapper over existing machinery, so there is no unjustified thin layer to challenge.
